items.title: The spherical mean identity behind the wave equation
items.statement: Let $c>0$, let $f\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ (unbounded $f$ is allowed), and define the spherical mean $$M_rf(x)=\frac1{4\pi}\int_{S^2}f(x+rn)\,d\Omega(n),\qquad r\ge0,$$ with the outward sphere measure of total area $4\pi$ ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]). Then $r\mapsto M_rf(x)$ is smooth for $r\ge0$ and satisfies the Euler-Poisson-Darboux identity $$\partial_r^2M_rf(x)+\frac2r\partial_rM_rf(x)=\Delta M_rf(x)\qquad(r>0),$$ and the function $H_f(x,t)=t\,M_{ct}f(x)$, $t\ge0$, satisfies $$\partial_t^2H_f=c^2\Delta H_f,\qquad H_f(x,0)=0,\qquad \partial_tH_f(x,0)=f(x).$$ All identities are local and need no decay of $f$, since every integration set is compact. This is the pure spherical-mean identity; it makes no claim about finite-domain boundary data or about general rough data.
items.strategy:
Differentiating the compact sphere integral in the parameter $r$ is justified by the parameter-integral lemma ([[lem-em-parameter-integrals]], including its surface-measure form). One gets $\partial_rM_rf(x)=(4\pi)^{-1}\int_{S^2}n\cdot
abla f(x+rn)\,d\Omega$, and the divergence theorem on $B_r(x)$ ([[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-piecewise-c-one-domains]], applied to the $C^1$ field $
abla f$ and using the Euclidean Laplacian, [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]) gives $4\pi r^2\partial_rM_rf(x)=\int_{B_r(x)}\Delta f(y)\,dy$. Differentiating this last integral in $r$ (radial derivative of a ball integral; one-variable fundamental theorem, [[thm-ftc-first-part]]) gives $\partial_r(r^2\partial_rM_rf)=r^2M_r(\Delta f)=r^2\Delta M_rf$, where the second equality uses linearity and the parameter statement to move $\Delta$ through the mean; dividing by $r^2$ gives the Euler-Poisson-Darboux identity. Twice differentiating $H_f(x,t)=tM_{ct}f(x)$ with the algebra of derivatives and the chain rule factor $c$ ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]) gives $\partial_t^2H_f=2c\partial_rM+c^2t\partial_r^2M=c^2t\Delta M=c^2\Delta H_f$ for $t>0$, using the identity just proved; at $t=0$ one has $M_0f=f$ and $\partial_rM_0f=(4\pi)^{-1}
abla f\cdot\int_{S^2}n\,d\Omega=0$ by reflection symmetry, so $H_f(x,0)=0$ and $\partial_tH_f(x,0)=f(x)$; the defining compact integral is smooth in signed $r$ as well, so the equation extends to $t=0$.

items.title: Ball Poisson series: interior convergence, boundary data and the Poisson kernel
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), with the exact meaning of [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $f\in L^2(S^2,d\Omega)$ with harmonic coefficients $f_{lm}$ in an orthonormal basis of the spherical-harmonic lemma ([[lem-em-spherical-harmonic-basis-and-addition]]), and for $0\le r<1$ set $u(rn)=\sum_{l,m}r^lf_{lm}Y_{lm}(n)$ (the $l=0$ term being the constant value at $r=0$). Then the series and all its derivatives converge uniformly on every closed smaller ball, $u$ is harmonic there ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]), $u(r\,\cdot)\to f$ in $L^2(S^2)$ as $r\uparrow1$, and $u$ is the unique harmonic function on the unit ball with $\sup_{r<1}\|u(r\,\cdot)\|_{L^2}<\infty$ and $L^2$ boundary limit $f$. For continuous $f$ the same function is $$u(rn)=\int_{S^2}\frac{1-r^2}{4\pi|rn-n'|^3}f(n')\,d\Omega(n'),$$ it extends continuously to the closed ball with boundary value $f$, and the kernel is positive of total mass one. This is the stated ball boundary branch; generic smooth-domain classical regularity remains a separate obligation.
items.strategy:
Fix the canonical real spherical-harmonic basis of [[lem-em-spherical-harmonic-basis-and-addition]]. Its complete orthonormality gives norm convergence and Parseval directly: the finite orthogonal projection S_N has ||f-S_N||2 no larger than ||f-v||2 for every finite-span v in its subspace, by finite Pythagoras; density therefore makes this error vanish. No arbitrary sequence of approximants is selected. The addition identity gives sum_m|Y_lm(n)|²=(2l+1)/(4pi). Finite and then countable Cauchy-Schwarz gives the absolute series tail bound $\|f\|_2[\sum_{l>N}r_0^{2l}(2l+1)/(4\pi)]^{1/2}$ on r<=r0<1. The terms r^lY_lm are actual homogeneous harmonic polynomials, including their smooth values at0. On a smaller ball use harmonic partial-sum differences on fixed-radius balls inside an intermediate smaller ball; the exact [[thm-interior-derivative-estimates-for-harmonic-functions]] converts the uniform tail bound into a uniform bound for every derivative. Uniform derivative limits are identified by the finite-coordinate FTC [[thm-newton-leibniz-with-interior-derivative]], yielding a smooth harmonic limit.

Orthogonality gives $\|u(r\cdot)\|_2^2=\sum_{l,m}r^{2l}|f_{lm}|^2\le\|f\|_2^2$ and $\|u(r\cdot)-f\|_2^2=\sum_{l,m}(1-r^l)^2|f_{lm}|^2$. The latter tends to0 by [[thm-dominated-convergence]] on the countable coefficient index set with counting measure and summable bound4sum|f_lm|².

The corrected generating kernel and addition identity sum the Poisson series as $P_r(n,n')=(1-r²)/(4\pi|rn-n'|³)$: apply (1+2r partial_r) to the scalar generating function, justified on every r<=r0<1 by its derived power series. Positivity is explicit and integration in nprime leaves only the constant harmonic, so the total mass is1. For continuous f, integrating the uniformly convergent kernel series gives precisely u. The actual [[thm-dirichlet-problem-on-a-ball-by-the-poisson-integral]] (n3, Countable Choice) proves its continuous extension and the classical uniqueness for continuous data.

For general L2-boundary uniqueness, let v be any smooth harmonic function on the unit ball with the stated radial norm bound and L2 limit f. For0<r<s<1, apply the same published continuous Dirichlet theorem on radius-s ball to the continuous actual data v(s n). Scale x=s z and sphere surface measure by s²; the resulting unit angular Poisson kernel is P_(r/s). Expanding that kernel and using orthogonality gives $v_{lm}(r)=(r/s)^l v_{lm}(s)$. The L2 boundary limit implies $v_{lm}(s)\to f_{lm}$ by Cauchy-Schwarz as s tends1. Thus $v_{lm}(r)=r^l f_{lm}$ for every degree and every fixed r>0. Completeness gives v(r dot)=u(r dot) in L2, and continuity on that sphere makes equality pointwise; equality at0 follows by continuity. This proves the full uniqueness branch without invoking an undeclared polar-Laplacian or radial ODE theorem. Countable Choice is inherited by the actual harmonic, finite-surface and L2 approximation suppliers, with no additional Dependent Choice or full Choice use.

references.title: Sheldon Axler, Paul Bourdon, Wade Ramey, Harmonic Function Theory, 2nd edition, author-hosted full text
references.locator: Full260-page author PDF retrieved and relevant Chapter5 sections inspected: printed78-82 (orthogonal spherical decomposition),94-100 (zonal harmonic projection/addition/Poisson expansion). items.title: Exact Helmholtz boundary representation with actual traces
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), with the exact meaning of [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded C-infinity domain of [[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]], let k>0 and x in Omega, and use the outgoing kernel $G_k$ of [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]]. A sufficient classical specialization is that u and f extend smoothly to an open neighbourhood of the closed domain and $(-\Delta-k^2)u=f$ there. More generally, retain the justified weaker classical-trace branch: u is C2 inside Omega, u and all first derivatives extend continuously to its closure, f=(-Delta-k²)u belongs to L1(Omega), and the equation holds inside. The boundary values and normal derivative in the formula below are these actual continuous traces. Then
$$u(x)=\int_\Omega G_k(x-y)f(y)\,dy+\int_{\partial\Omega}\bigl[G_k(x-y)\partial_nu(y)-u(y)\partial_{n_y}G_k(x-y)\bigr]dS_y,$$
with n the outward domain normal; both integrals are absolutely convergent. Merely being smooth on the OPEN domain without these trace/integrability data is insufficient.

For an exterior D=R3 minus closure of a bounded smooth obstacle, retain the exterior counterpart with actual inner boundary traces: suppose u is C2 on D with u and first derivatives continuous to its compact boundary, solves (-Delta-k²)u=f there, f is locally continuous and $\int_D|G_k(x-y)f(y)|dy$ is finite at the observation x, and the prescribed outgoing condition gives, uniformly on spheres at infinity, $u(y)=O(|y|^{-1})$ and $\partial_ru(y)-iku(y)=o(|y|^{-1})$. Then the same formula holds with volume D and its obstacle boundary, with n outward from D (pointing into the obstacle). Compactly supported L1 sources with the displayed local regularity are a sufficient source subclass. For the smooth-trace modal outgoing specialization beyond a source-containing sphere of radius $R_0>0$, retain the declared full Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) for this sufficient branch. Write the smooth angular trace as $g(n)=u(R_0n)$, use the real unit-sphere harmonics of [[lem-em-spherical-harmonic-basis-and-addition]], set $c_{lm}=\int_{S^2}g(n)Y_{lm}(n)d\Omega(n)$, and define the outgoing modal class outside that sphere by
$$u(rn)=\sum_{l=0}^\infty\sum_{m=1}^{2l+1}c_{lm}\,\frac{h_l(kr)}{h_l(kR_0)}Y_{lm}(n),\qquad r\ge R_0,$$
where $h_l$ are exactly the earlier explicit functions of [[lem-em-outgoing-spherical-hankel-dtn-bounds]]. The proof below establishes smooth convergence, the homogeneous exterior equation, the actual trace g, the uniform bound $\sup_{r\ge R_0,n\in S^2}r|u(rn)|<\infty$ and the uniform Sommerfeld residual $\sup_{n\in S^2}r|\partial_ru(rn)-iku(rn)|\to0$. Thus this existing smooth modal branch satisfies the prescribed far conditions without a later same-page supplier. Its full-Choice premise is retained; the earlier prescribed-outgoing branch remains under Countable Choice.

The Green formula uses the consistent actual pair of traces. Assigning both aperture values independently does not establish an exact boundary problem; a declared scalar aperture-source model remains a separate approximation. No weak boundary trace or normal trace for arbitrary rough data is asserted by mere interior smoothness.
items.strategy:
For the closure-smooth bounded specialization, apply [[cor-second-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] on Omega with a small ball about x removed. The k² terms cancel, the outgoing kernel's unit inner flux gives u(x), and its derivative-test term is O(delta); the source integral near x is finite since f is continuous there and G_k is locally integrable. This proves the stated signs.

For the weaker C2-interior/C1-closure trace branch, let S be the compact smooth boundary with its outward normal n. The exact [[thm-euclidean-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem]] under Countable Choice gives a normal tube with positive smooth radius; compactness gives a positive minimum. For sufficiently small t>0, $S_t=\{p-t n(p):p\in S\}$ lies inside Omega and bounds the inner domain Omega_t. In the normal graph charts the surface Jacobian and outward normals converge uniformly to those on S (the differential of p to p-tn(p) tends uniformly to the tangent identity). The one-sided graph convention makes this the actual inside collar; injectivity of the tube prevents overlap. For small t, x and a fixed ball about x lie in Omega_t. On each punctured Omega_t the ordinary Green theorem applies, since u is C2 on a neighbourhood of its compact closure. First remove the x-excision radius by the same local flux argument. Then take t down0: u and its gradient converge uniformly on S_t to their continuous actual traces, while G_k and its y-gradient are bounded and smooth on this collar away from x. The boundary integrals therefore converge to exactly the displayed trace integrals using the compact surface chart formula and the uniformly converging Jacobians. For the volume term, split off a small ball about x, where f is bounded and the kernel is integrable; on its complement G_k is bounded and f is L1. This gives an absolute integrable majorant, so [[thm-dominated-convergence]] on the increasing inner domains yields the full volume integral. This proves the weaker branch completely rather than assuming unspecified traces.

For the exterior branch, truncate by B_R and use the same inner-boundary trace limit and x-excision argument, with the outward obstacle normal pointing into the obstacle. For fixed observation x, on y=Rn the explicit kernel has $G_k(x-y)=O(R^{-1})$ and $\partial_R G_k(x-y)-ikG_k(x-y)=O(R^{-2})$, uniformly in n; these follow by differentiating the norm and $\partial_R|Rn-x|=1+O(R^{-2})$. In the outer Wronskian, write $G_k(\partial_Ru-iku)-u(\partial_RG_k-ikG_k)$: its supremum is o(R^-2)+O(R^-3), so multiplying by the sphere area O(R²) makes it tend to0. Absolute convergence of the stated volume integral then permits the limit R to infinity. The smooth-trace modal outgoing subclass has the explicit earlier-supplier proof below; its existing full-Choice sufficient premise is retained. Other prescribed uniform-outgoing data use only Countable Choice through Green, tubular and surface interfaces. No independent assignment of both boundary traces or unproved rough-trace Green theorem is used. The cited Green theorem has real inputs; apply it to the four real/imaginary component pairs and combine by complex bilinearity to obtain the displayed complex kernel identity, with no conjugation introduced.

Smooth angular coefficient estimate from finite angular calculus. For smooth w on S2 let $L_jw(n)=\left.\frac{d}{dt}w(Q_j(t)n)\right|_{t=0}$, where $Q_j(t)$ is the elementary coordinate rotation about e_j, and put $\Lambda=\sum_{j=1}^3L_j^2$. Its tangent velocity is $e_j\times n$ with [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]. Rotation invariance of surface measure is the exact earlier [[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]]. Differentiate the invariant integral of w(Q_j(t)n)v(Q_j(t)n) on the compact sphere: uniform difference quotients of its smooth integrand give $\int(L_jw)v=-\int w(L_jv)$, so Lambda is symmetric under the bilinear integral; for complex data apply the same finite identity to components. No polar-operator theorem is presumed. On an ambient smooth extension, direct coordinate differentiation gives
$$\sum_jL_j^2=|x|^2\Delta-(x\cdot\nabla)^2-x\cdot\nabla.$$
Each Y_lm is the restriction of a degree-l homogeneous harmonic polynomial by the earlier H2 supplier, so Euler's identity and this finite formula give $\Lambda Y_{lm}=-l(l+1)Y_{lm}$. Therefore, for l>=1 and any integer p>=1, repeated symmetry and [[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]] yield
$$[l(l+1)]^p c_{lm}=\int_{S^2}(-\Lambda)^pg\,Y_{lm}\,d\Omega,\qquad |c_{lm}|\le\frac{\|\Lambda^pg\|_2}{[l(l+1)]^p}.$$
The smooth g and all these angular derivatives are bounded on the compact sphere and have finite L2 norms. Treat l0 separately as its single finite constant coefficient. The addition diagonal of H2 gives $\|Y_{lm}\|_\infty\le\sqrt{(2l+1)/(4\pi)}$. With p2, the total weighted absolute sum
$$\sum_{l,m}(l+1+2kR_0)|c_{lm}|\,\|Y_{lm}\|_\infty<\infty$$
follows: for l>=1 its degree-l bound is a fixed constant times $(2l+1)(l+1+2kR_0)\sqrt{(2l+1)/(4\pi)}[l(l+1)]^{-2}=O(l^{-3/2})$. This is the actual summability argument for every smooth trace, not an unproved claim of coefficient decay.

Exact radial majorants. From the earlier Hankel proof, $F_l(z)=z^2|h_l(z)|^2=\sum_{j=0}^la_jz^{-2j}$ has a0=1 and positive a_j, so it is nonincreasing in z>0. Consequently, for $\phi_l(r)=h_l(kr)/h_l(kR_0)$,
$$|\phi_l(r)|\le R_0/r\quad(r\ge R_0).$$
The same earlier supplier's exact t_l bounds, applied with radius r, give $|k h_l'(kr)/h_l(kr)|\le(l+1)/r+k$, hence
$$r|\phi_l'(r)-ik\phi_l(r)|\le R_0[(l+1)/r+2k]\le l+1+2kR_0.$$
For every FIXED l the explicit finite outgoing polynomial gives $r(\phi_l'-ik\phi_l)\to0$ as r tends infinity. The weighted coefficient sum therefore bounds every residual tail uniformly for ALL r>=R0 and n on the sphere. Given epsilon, choose a finite degree cutoff making that tail smaller than epsilon/2; the finitely many remaining radial residuals tend to0 uniformly after multiplication by their fixed finite angular suprema. This finite-head/finite-tail argument proves the uniform Sommerfeld limit. Also $r|u(rn)|\le R_0\sum|c_{lm}|\|Y_{lm}\|_\infty$ uniformly, which proves exactly the amplitude bound used in the outer Green Wronskian. The first radial derivative series is uniformly convergent on r>=R0 since $|\phi_l'|\le[(l+1)/R_0+k]|\phi_l|$ and the same weighted sum dominates it; finite-coordinate FTC [[thm-newton-leibniz-with-interior-derivative]] identifies that derivative with partial_r u.

Smooth modal realization and normalization. Rotational differentiation preserves the degree-l harmonic space. Skew symmetry gives $\sum_j\|L_jv\|_2^2=l(l+1)\|v\|_2^2$ in that finite space, so each successive angular derivative has norm at most [l(l+1)]^(1/2) times the preceding norm. Its pointwise norm is bounded by sqrt((2l+1)/(4pi)) times its L2 norm by finite basis Cauchy-Schwarz and the addition identity. The radial ODE of the earlier Hankel supplier, differentiated finitely many times, gives for every fixed q a bound $|\phi_l^{(q)}(r)|\le C_{q,k,R_0}(l+1)^{2q}/r$ on r>=R0: q0 is the radial-ratio bound, q1 is the logarithmic-derivative bound, and the equation plus derivatives of r^-1,r^-2 gives the induction. Thus every radial/angular derivative series is dominated by a finite power of l times the coefficient estimate with a sufficiently large p. It converges uniformly on each closed bounded exterior annulus; FTC identifies all derivatives. Cartesian derivatives there are finite combinations of radial and angular derivatives with smooth coefficients (from $\nabla=n\partial_r-r^{-1}n\times(L_1,L_2,L_3)$), so the series defines a smooth exterior field. The finite angular identity above gives the polar Laplacian formula on phi_l(r)Y_lm, and the radial ODE makes each term solve (Delta+k²)u0; termwise second derivatives prove the equation for the limit. At rR0 the absolute series has its L2 coefficients c_lm; completeness of H2 and continuity give its actual smooth trace g. If trace coefficients are recorded instead in the sphere-normalized basis $Y^{R_0}_{lm}(R_0n)=R_0^{-1}Y_{lm}(n)$, their coefficients are R0 c_lm, so the displayed expansion is identical after normalization. No weaker rough-trace claim or obstacle-boundary existence is inferred. All bounded Green, weaker C1-trace, exterior source and smooth-modal conclusions are preserved, with the same declared Choice strengths.

items.title: Weak Dirichlet problem with prescribed fractional Sobolev boundary data
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice as declared by the trace and Sobolev suppliers. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^1$ domain, let $\varepsilon$ be a measurable symmetric uniformly elliptic coefficient as in the lift lemma ([[lem-em-lift-specified-dirichlet-existence]]), let $\rho\in L^2(\Omega)$, and prescribe $g\in H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)=W^{1/2,2}(\partial\Omega)$, the fractional Sobolev space of the boundary definition, defined by a finite graph atlas and partition with norm given by the finite sums of localised $L^2$ norms and Gagliardo seminorms ([[def-fractional-sobolev-space-on-a-compact-c-one-boundary]], [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]). Then there is exactly one $u\in H^1(\Omega)$ with trace $Tu=g$ solving $$\int_\Omega\nabla v\cdot\varepsilon\nabla u=\int_\Omega\rho\,v\qquad\text{for every }v\in H_0^1(\Omega),$$ and the solution depends continuously on $(\rho,g)$: $\|u\|_{H^1}\le C(\|\rho\|_{L^2}+\|g\|_{H^{1/2}})$. The prescribed trace is exact and no classical $C^2$ boundary regularity is inferred.
items.strategy: The sharp trace theorem and its bounded right inverse ([[thm-sharp-trace-theorem-for-w-one-p]], [[thm-bounded-right-inverse-for-the-sobolev-trace]]) give a bounded linear $R:H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)\to H^1(\Omega)$ with $TRg=g$; the flat half-space estimates are the normal-line and Hardy estimates exposed in the research argument. The kernel of the trace is $H_0^1(\Omega)$ ([[thm-kernel-of-the-trace-is-w-one-p-zero]], with the zero-boundary Sobolev space defined as a closure), so $u=Rg+w$ with $w\in H_0^1$; applying the lift lemma with $G=Rg$ ([[lem-em-lift-specified-dirichlet-existence]]) gives the unique $w$ and hence existence, exact trace and uniqueness. Continuous dependence follows from the estimates of the lift and solver lemmas together with the boundedness of $R$: for two data sets, $\|\nabla(w_1-w_2)\|_2\le\alpha^{-1}[2L\|\rho_1-\rho_2\|_2+\beta\|\nabla R(g_1-g_2)\|_2]$, and the $H^1$ estimate follows by adding $\|Rg\|_{H^1}\le C\|g\|_{H^{1/2}}$.

items.title: Outgoing spherical trace and Dirichlet-to-Neumann map
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the explicitly used trace and weak Dirichlet-solvability suppliers. Let $k>0$ and $R>0$. Use the sphere-normalised basis $Y^R_{lm}(Rn):=R^{-1}Y_{lm}(n)$ on $S_R$, where $Y_{lm}$ is the complete normalised unit-sphere basis of the spherical-harmonic lemma ([[lem-em-spherical-harmonic-basis-and-addition]]) and the coefficients $t_l$ of the outgoing radial-function lemma ([[lem-em-outgoing-spherical-hankel-dtn-bounds]]). The map $$T_Rf=\sum_{l,m}t_l\,f_{lm}Y^R_{lm},\qquad f\in H^{1/2}(S_R),$$ is a bounded linear operator $H^{1/2}(S_R)\to H^{-1/2}(S_R)$ with $$\operatorname{Re}\langle T_Rf,f\rangle\le0,\qquad \operatorname{Im}\langle T_Rf,f\rangle=\sum_{l,m}(\operatorname{Im}t_l)|f_{lm}|^2>0\ \ (f\ne0).$$ It is precisely the outgoing scalar Helmholtz normal derivative at $r=R$: for every $f\in H^{1/2}(S_R)$ the function $u(rn)=\sum_{l,m}f_{lm}h_l(kr)/h_l(kR)\,R^{-1}Y_{lm}(n)$ for $r\ge R$ is the unique outgoing finite-local-energy exterior solution with trace $f$ on $S_R$ and normal derivative $T_Rf$ in the weak trace sense; it is smooth away from the sphere, and for smooth $f$ it satisfies the ordinary Sommerfeld condition. No uniform pointwise outgoing condition is asserted for arbitrary rough traces; the outgoing condition there is its modal/weak version. Here finite-local-energy means membership in $H^1(\{R<|x|<R_1\})$ for every finite $R_1>R$, with the $H^{1/2}$ trace on $S_R$; no global $H^1$ or global $L^2$ condition at infinity is imposed. The outgoing modal class consists of the displayed outgoing $h_l$ radial factors with no incoming partners; for rough traces this modal class is the definition, rather than a pointwise Sommerfeld assertion. Here the boundary Sobolev spaces are their complex versions (or complexifications of the real trace spaces), $f_{lm}=\int_{S_R}f\overline{Y^R_{lm}}\,d\sigma_R$, and the DtN dual pairing is linear in its first argument and conjugate-linear in its second.
items.strategy: The boundary norm of the fractional Sobolev space is equivalent, for fixed $R$, to $\sum_{l,m}(l+1)|f_{lm}|^2$: for finite harmonic data the harmonic ball extension $\sum_{l,m}(r/R)^lf_{lm}R^{-1}Y_{lm}(n)$ has Dirichlet energy $\sum(l/R)|f_{lm}|^2$ by the first Green identity ([[cor-first-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]) and normal differentiation, and $L^2$ ball norm $\sum R/(2l+3)|f_{lm}|^2$ with the sphere-normalised basis, so its $H^1$ norm is equivalent to $\sum(l+1)|f_{lm}|^2$. For arbitrary $H^{1/2}$ data the bounded right inverse and the weak harmonic Dirichlet solver of the prescribed-data lemma ([[lem-em-prescribed-fractional-dirichlet-existence]]) give a controlled harmonic $H^1$ extension; the harmonic coefficients and orthogonality of the ball Poisson series lemma ([[lem-em-ball-poisson-series-boundary-convergence]]) show the finite energy partial sums are bounded by its energy, giving both directions of the equivalence. The bounds $|t_l|\le(l+1)/R+k$ of the spherical Hankel lemma ([[lem-em-outgoing-spherical-hankel-dtn-bounds]]) make $T_R$ bounded into the dual weighted space, and the real and imaginary pairings converge with the stated signs, strict positivity following from $\operatorname{Im}t_l>0$ for every $l$. For the exterior realisation, define $u_{lm}(r)=f_{lm}h_l(kr)/h_l(kR)$, $r\ge R$; the finite polynomial positive formula gives $|h_l(kr)/h_l(kR)|\le R/r$ and, by the recurrence, geometric-in-$l$ radial ratios on every compact $r>R$ interval, so the series and all derivatives converge uniformly there, away from the sphere; the smoothness, the weak trace identification and the annular $H^1$ control follow from Green's identity for each mode on $[R,R+\delta]$ and the bounds above. Uniqueness: the general radial Helmholtz solutions are multiples of $h_l(kr)$ and its incoming partner, whose Wronskian is nonzero; Sommerfeld selects $h_l$, and harmonic completeness forces any smooth outgoing exterior solution to have exactly this map. The annular $H^1$ estimates are precisely the finite-local-energy condition; they do not assert global integrability at infinity. At $l=0$, a nonzero outgoing mode is proportional to $e^{ikr}/r$ and its global $L^2$ norm diverges, which confirms why no global energy condition is imposed. Both the ball and exterior radial extensions use $R^{-1}Y_{lm}(n)$ explicitly; the sphere-normalisation is $Y^R_{lm}(Rn)=R^{-1}Y_{lm}(n)$, giving the stated radial ball-norm factor $R/(2l+3)$ for the sphere-normalised coefficients. For complex boundary data, apply the real prescribed-trace/harmonic solver to the real and imaginary parts and combine; the resulting squared norm is the sum of the two real energy norms, with the stated sesquilinear pairing.

items.title: Weak Neumann and transmission existence with interface charges
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice for the actually cited Sobolev trace, lift and mean-zero density interfaces, and its Countable Choice consequence for the measure and variational interfaces ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded connected $C^1$ domain, let $\varepsilon$ be measurable symmetric uniformly elliptic, let $ho\in L^2(\Omega)$, and let $g\in H^{-1/2}(\partial\Omega)$, the bounded real dual of the boundary trace space ([[def-fractional-sobolev-space-on-a-compact-c-one-boundary]]). Define $\ell(v)=\int_\Omegaho v+\langle g,Tvangle$ on $H^1(\Omega)$ ([[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]). A weak Neumann solution is a $u\in H^1$ with $$\int_\Omega
abla v\cdot\varepsilon
abla u=\ell(v)\qquad	ext{for every }v\in H^1(\Omega).$$ Such a solution exists if and only if $\ell(1)=0$, and is then unique up to an additive constant; normalising $\int_\Omega u=0$ makes it unique. On finitely many connected components the compatibility and normalisation are imposed separately on each component. For finitely many disjoint smooth stationary interfaces with piecewise smooth uniformly elliptic $\varepsilon$, bulk data $ho\in L^2$ and prescribed sheet charge $\sigma$ on the interfaces defining a bounded trace functional on $H^1$ (for instance $\sigma\in L^2$ of each smooth compact interface), the same argument gives weak Dirichlet or compatible Neumann existence for the transmission problem, with the globally $H^1$ potential having identical one-sided trace; where the solution is classically smooth on each side, integration by parts gives the jump $n\cdot[\varepsilon
abla u]=-\sigma$, equivalently $n\cdot[D]=\sigma$ for the explicitly defined mathematical flux $D:=-\varepsilon
abla u$ on each side. General piecewise classical regularity remains a separate requirement.
items.strategy:
Full AC is inherited from [[lem-em-prescribed-fractional-dirichlet-existence]], [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] and [[lem-em-mean-zero-coercivity-on-a-c-one-domain]]; the symmetric minimising-sequence solver itself needs only Countable Choice. No stronger choice principle is used. The trace bound of the prescribed-data lemma and Holder's inequality make $|\ell(v)|\le C\|v\|_{H^1}$ ([[lem-em-prescribed-fractional-dirichlet-existence]], [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]], [[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]]). Testing the equation with $v=1$ makes $\ell(1)=0$ necessary. The mean-zero subspace of $H^1$ is closed, and the mean-zero coercivity lemma makes its gradient norm equivalent to the complete $H^1$ norm ([[lem-em-mean-zero-coercivity-on-a-c-one-domain]]); the symmetric coercive variational solver ([[lem-em-symmetric-coercive-variational-solver]]) solves the coercive symmetric form there. Every $v\in H^1$ is its mean-zero part plus a constant, and the constant term contributes zero on both sides by compatibility, so this solves the full problem; for the difference of two solutions tested against itself the gradient vanishes, and the mean-zero inequality makes the difference constant. Each finite disjoint component is treated separately. The transmission case replaces $\ell$ by the sum of the bulk, boundary and interface trace functionals of the prescribed sheet charge; the same variational argument applies, and the one-sided trace identity holds for the globally $H^1$ potential by trace continuity in each chart, giving the stated jump relation where the solution is classically smooth on each side. In the classical jump equivalence define $D:=-\varepsilon
abla u$ piecewise; then $[D]=-[\varepsilon
abla u]$, so $n\cdot[\varepsilon
abla u]=-\sigma$ is exactly $n\cdot[D]=\sigma$. Here $D$ is a mathematical flux vector, not an undeclared physical displacement field.

items.title: A fixed smooth-domain extension that preserves smooth parameters
items.statement:
Let `Omega⊂R3` be a bounded smooth graph domain. Choose an open spatial neighbourhood `V` of its compact closure. There exists a fixed real linear spatial extension operator `E_Omega`, determined only by the domain, finite charts and cutoffs, with this parameter property. For every open interval `J` and function `u:Omega×J→R` that is smooth in the interior and whose every mixed derivative has a continuous extension to `closure Omega × J`, the function `E_Omega u` is `C∞` on `R3×J`, equals `u` and all its continuous boundary jets on `closure Omega × J`, and is supported spatially in one fixed compact subset of `V`. For every compact `K⊂J`, integer `m≥0` and `j≥0`,

$$\sup_{t\in K}\|\partial_t^j E_\Omega u(\cdot,t)\|_{C^m(\mathbb R^3)}\le C_m\sup_{t\in K}\|\partial_t^j u(\cdot,t)\|_{C^m(\overline\Omega)}.$$

The `C^m` seminorm is the finite sum of suprema of spatial derivatives through order `m`. The extension commutes with every time derivative; charts and coefficients do not depend on `t`. No uniform bound over all of an unbounded `J` is assumed. Vector-valued inputs of finite dimension are extended componentwise. This construction adds no choice principle: a finite atlas can be selected from the cover of all admissible chart patches, finite cutoffs are supplied by the published finite-partition/cutoff lemmas, and the infinite coefficient sequence is defined explicitly below. The consuming elliptic/Sobolev argument retains its already-declared AC assumptions.
items.strategy:
**1. Explicit coefficients; no unproved moment lemma.** Put `b_k=−2^k`, `k=0,1,...`. For `N≥k` define

$$a_k^{(N)}=\prod_{\substack{0\le j\le N\\j\ne k}}\frac{1-b_j}{b_k-b_j},\qquad a_k=\lim_{N\to\infty}a_k^{(N)}.$$

The factors for `j<k` have sign negative, those for `j>k` positive; the sign is `(-1)^k`. For every finite index set, `prod(1+2^{-j})≤6`: the factors `j=0,1` give 3, and for the tail `j≥2`, the sum of `2^{-j}` is at most `1/2`, while the elementary induction `prod(1+x_j)≤1/(1−sum x_j)` bounds that tail by 2. Similarly `prod_{l=1}^M(1−2^{-l})≥1/4`: separate the first factor `1/2`, and use `prod(1−x_j)≥1−sum x_j≥1/2` on `l≥2`. The geometric-series supplier gives the stated sums, including their starting indices.

For `j<k` the absolute product is

$$2^{-k(k+1)/2}\frac{\prod_{j<k}(1+2^{-j})}{\prod_{l=1}^{k}(1-2^{-l})};$$

for `j>k` it is `prod_{j=k+1}^N(1+2^{-j})/prod_{l=1}^{N-k}(1−2^{-l})`. Thus

$$|a_k^{(N)}|\le576\,2^{-k(k+1)/2}\qquad(N\ge k).$$

At fixed `k`, the positive absolute value increases with `N`, since every new tail factor is greater than one, and it is bounded by this displayed constant. The published real monotone convergence theorem gives the limit `a_k`, with the same bound and sign. This defines every coefficient without selecting unspecified sequences.

For each integer `r≥0`, finite interpolation gives `sum_{k=0}^N a_k^{(N)} b_k^r=1` when `N≥r`: the polynomial

$$z^r-\sum_{k=0}^N b_k^r\prod_{\substack{0\le j\le N\\j\ne k}}\frac{z-b_j}{b_k-b_j}$$

has degree at most `N` and vanishes at the `N+1` distinct nodes `b_0,...,b_N`, so is zero by the exact published real-polynomial root bound; evaluate at `z=1`. To pass to the limit, the bound above gives `|a_k^{(N)} b_k^r|≤576·2^{-k(k+1)/2+kr}` uniformly in `N`. For `k≥2r+1` this is at most `576·2^{-k}`, whose tail tends to zero. First cut the sum at a fixed `M`, pass to the limit in those finitely many coefficients, and then let `M` increase. This proves both

$$\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}a_k b_k^r=1,\qquad\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}|a_k|\,|b_k|^r<\infty\quad(r\ge0).$$

No original Seeley coefficient existence assertion is used as an unproved prerequisite.

**2. One flattened patch, with arbitrary parameters.** Write a smooth boundary patch as `(y,s)`, `s>0` inside the domain. A localized input `w(y,s,t)` has spatial support compactly inside the ambient chart, separated from its artificial edges, and every mixed derivative extends continuously to `s=0`. Extend it by zero at the artificial positive-side edges to the half-space. Choose a fixed smooth real normal cutoff `rho` that equals 1 near 0 and vanishes for `s≥delta/2`, with `delta` small enough that all sampled positive collar points remain in the chart. Define

$$\mathcal Ew(y,s,t)=w(y,s,t)\ (s\ge0),\qquad\mathcal Ew(y,s,t)=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}a_k\rho(b_ks)w(y,b_ks,t)\ (s<0).$$

For fixed negative `s`, the sum is locally finite because `b_k s=2^k|s|` eventually exceeds the cutoff support. It is therefore smooth off `s=0`. For any normal order `r`, tangential multi-index `alpha`, time order `j`, and compact parameter/tangential set, its termwise derivative for `s<0` is

$$a_k b_k^r\,[\partial_z^r\partial_y^\alpha\partial_t^j(\rho(z)w(y,z,t))]_{z=b_ks}.$$

On the fixed compact collar and a compact `K⊂J`, every input derivative in this formula is bounded; the supremum of the sum is bounded by a finite cutoff-dependent constant times `sum|a_k||b_k|^r`. The bounds hold locally uniformly up to `s=0`, with the **same** compact time set `K`; only the normal spatial argument is sampled.

As `s↑0`, for each fixed term the normal cutoff is identically one and all its positive-order derivatives vanish. The derivative therefore tends to `a_k b_k^r partial_s^r partial_y^alpha partial_t^j w(y,0,t)`. The finite-head/uniform-tail argument using the weighted absolute sum proves uniform convergence of the boundary limit on compact `(y,t)` sets. The moment identity then makes that limit exactly the input boundary derivative. This establishes matching continuous derivatives of every mixed order; no derivative of an infinite nonuniformly convergent series is assumed at the boundary.

**3. Matching jets imply actual joint smoothness.** For a function glued from the two sides, matching values give continuity. If the side first partial derivatives extend continuously and agree, the normal coordinate-segment FTC, on either side and up to `s=0`, proves the derivative at `s=0` equals their common limit. For tangential or time segments at `s=0`, first write the coordinate-segment FTC at `s≠0`, then let `s→0`; uniform convergence on the compact segment passes the integral to the common continuous boundary derivative. FTC again gives that tangential/time derivative on `s=0`. Thus the glued function is `C1` jointly. Apply the same argument successively to the already-matched derivatives of orders 1,2,... to obtain `C∞` on the ambient patch × `J`. The input itself obeys those boundary segment identities by the same limit from its positive side. This is a complete smooth-gluing argument, not a reference to a Whitney extension theorem.

The derivative bound at total spatial order `m` uses only input derivatives through `m`, with `sum|a_k|2^{km}` finite and the fixed cutoff derivatives through `m`. The operator is linear and does not change the time argument, so the time-commutation identity and the stated local seminorm estimate follow.

**4. Finite chart gluing on the fixed smooth domain.** Choose finitely many shrunk smooth graph charts and an interior open patch. Compactness gives finitely many smaller balls covering the domain closure, with their closed larger balls contained in the assigned chart/interior open members. Using the choice-free Euclidean compact cutoff supplier, take smooth nonnegative psi_l equal to one on each smaller ball and supported in its larger ball. S=sum_l psi_l is positive on a neighbourhood of the closure. Choose a smooth outer cutoff chi equal to one near the closure and compactly supported in {S>0}. For each chart j set chi_j=chi(sum of psi_l assigned to j)/S on {S>0}, and zero elsewhere. These functions are smooth, have supports in the chart members, and sum to one near the closure. Only finitely many choices are made; no measure-convention partition theorem is used. Localize u by these fixed spatial cutoffs. The interior piece is supported away from the physical boundary and is extended by zero, preserving smoothness. Each boundary piece is pulled through its smooth chart and extended by the preceding formula. Choose a fixed outer chart cutoff equal to one on both the positive localized support and the small negative support created by the extension, with compact support inside the larger chart; multiply before pulling back. This makes each piece smooth across its artificial edges when extended by zero in ambient space. Such collar sizes and cutoffs are available by shrinking the finite compact patches. The extension's tangential support never leaves that of the localized piece, and its negative normal support stays within `|s|<delta/2`, so the claimed outer support control is genuine.

Pullback is smooth by repeated ordinary chain rule with chart derivatives bounded at each fixed order on those compact supports. Add the finitely many pieces. On the domain their sum is `u` by the partition identity; all boundary jets agree by continuity from the interior. Each support lies in a fixed compact subset of the prescribed `V`, so their finite union does too. The charts, partitions and coefficient sequence are independent of time. This proves the claimed single parameter-preserving operator and its `C^m` seminorm bounds; it introduces no temporal patch choices or global bounds on unbounded intervals.

items.title: Smooth parameter-dependent Dirichlet and compatible Neumann Poisson solvers
items.statement:
Assume AC and Countable Choice carried by the variational/Sobolev suppliers. Let `Omega` be a bounded smooth graph domain in `R3`, `epsilon>0` constant and `J` an open interval. Let the bulk datum `f` be jointly smooth up to `closure Omega×J` in the all-mixed-derivative sense of the first supplier, and let boundary families `g_D`, `kappa` be smooth in a fixed finite boundary atlas × `J`. Then the Dirichlet problem `−epsilon Delta u=f`, `u|boundary=g_D` has a unique solution on `Omega×J`; it has a single smooth ambient continuation near the closed spatial domain × `J`. The Neumann problem `−epsilon Delta u=f`, `epsilon partial_nu u=kappa` has such a solution precisely when

$$\int_{\Omega_j}f(\cdot,t)+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}\kappa(\cdot,t)=0\quad\text{for each component and every }t\in J.$$

It is unique modulo a separately chosen spatial constant on each component at each time. The normalization `integral_Omega_j u(·,t)=0` gives a unique smooth family. Both solution operations are linear in their data; time differentiation commutes with them. Smoothness and estimates are local in compact time subintervals, with no uniform-in-`J` requirement. The smooth ambient continuations are auxiliary and are not unique off the closed physical spatial region.
items.strategy:
**Fixed boundary lifts.** Use a finite boundary partition, graph coordinates `r=x3−h(y)`, with the domain on `r<0`, outward normal `nu=(-grad h,1)/sqrt(1+|grad h|²)`, and a fixed normal cutoff equal to one near 0. On a localized boundary datum `g_j(y,t)`, the Dirichlet lift is `rho(r)g_j(y,t)` with a larger fixed chart cutoff. For an outward conormal datum `kappa_j`, the Neumann lift is

$$L_N\kappa_j(y,r,t)=\frac{r\rho(r)\kappa_j(y,t)}{\epsilon\sqrt{1+|\nabla h(y)|^2}},$$

again with a fixed larger chart cutoff equal to one near the datum support. At `r=0`, the terms from differentiating the coefficient or cutoff vanish because of the factor `r`, while `partial_nu r=sqrt(1+|grad h|²)`; hence `epsilon partial_nu L_N kappa_j=kappa_j`. Add the finite chart pieces. The partition's boundary sum is one, so both lifts have the exact required datum. They are linear, independent of time, smooth in an actual spatial collar × `J`, and their spatial `H^{k+2}` norms are bounded by constants times finite `C^{k+2}` boundary seminorms. Choosing higher seminorm orders is allowed; no sharp boundary Sobolev norm is asserted. For Dirichlet, subtract the lift and apply the earlier zero-lift weak Dirichlet solver plus the exact published higher-order Dirichlet estimate to the source `f+epsilon Delta L_Dg_D`.

**Neumann weak existence and H1 bound.** The earlier weak Neumann lemma accepts the bulk `L2` datum and the bounded boundary trace functional, and proves necessity/sufficiency of componentwise compatibility. Smooth boundary `kappa` defines that bounded functional by Cauchy–Schwarz and the exact published `H1→L2(boundary)` trace theorem. Mean-zero coercivity on each component gives

$$\|u\|_{H^1}\le C_{\Omega,\epsilon}\bigl(\|f\|_2+\|\kappa\|_{L^2(\partial\Omega)}\bigr)$$

for the normalized solution, by testing against it and absorbing the gradient norm. A bounded smooth graph domain has only finitely many components: every bounded open component has boundary in the domain boundary; a finite cover by connected one-sided graph patches meets only finitely many components, and every component meets such a patch. Thus all normalizations and lift/estimate sums are finite. After subtracting `H=L_N kappa`, the residual `w=u−H` has homogeneous Neumann flux and source `f+epsilon Delta H`; its mean is the negative mean of `H`. The smooth first Green identity verifies the weak lift subtraction, and the divergence theorem verifies that its residual bulk integral is zero under the original compatibility. A constant normalization does not affect the flux or elliptic equation.

**Natural-boundary H2 estimate; explicit source terms.** Flatten the fixed smooth boundary and take a localized weak solution `z∈H1` supported away from artificial chart edges, whose weak equation, for supported `H1` tests including nonzero boundary trace, is

$$\int A_{ij}\partial_jz\partial_iv=\int p v+\int G_i\partial_iv,\quad p\in L^2,\ G\in H^1.$$

The smooth symmetric uniformly positive transformed `A` is the ordinary Jacobian/metric transform of the constant scalar operator. The original homogeneous-flux problem has `G=0`; localization by a spatial cutoff `eta` changes the scalar datum to `eta p−A grad z·grad eta+G·grad eta` and the vector datum to `eta G+z A grad eta`, still respectively `L2` and `H1`. These exact terms account for natural flux under localization; no false zero-trace condition is imposed.

For a tangential direction `k`, put `w_h=delta_h^k z` and test with `v=−delta_{−h}^k(eta² w_h)`. This is a supported `H1` test, allowed by the natural variational formulation; it need not vanish at the physical boundary. The published quotient integration-by-parts/product/weak-commutation identities give principal term `integral eta² A(y+h) grad w_h·grad w_h≥alpha||eta grad w_h||²`. The coefficient/cutoff remainders are exactly those of the usual quotient expansion and are bounded by `C||z||H1 (||eta grad w_h||2+||w_h||2)`, with `||w_h||2≤C||z||H1` and `||delta_h A||infinity≤||partial_k A||infinity`. The scalar datum contributes at most `C||p||2(||eta grad w_h||2+||w_h||2)` because the derivative quotient stays on the test, not on `p`. Discrete integration by parts moves the quotient in the vector datum term to `G`, whose contribution is

$$\left|\int\delta_h^kG\cdot\nabla(\eta^2w_h)\right|\le C\|G\|_{H^1}(\|\eta\nabla w_h\|_2+\|w_h\|_2).$$

Cauchy–Schwarz and Young absorption give a uniform bound `||eta grad delta_h^k z||2≤C(||p||2+||G||H1+||z||H1)`. Pass to test pairings; the quotient's limiting derivative is a bounded functional on the `L2` closure of compact tests, and Hilbert Riesz supplies its `L2` representative. This provides all second derivatives with a tangential factor, including mixed ones, without a weak-subsequence assumption. The distributional equation is `−div(A grad z)=p−div G`; therefore the normal derivative has the corrected identity

$$A_{33}\partial_{33}z=-p+\operatorname{div}G-\sum_{(i,j)\ne(3,3)}A_{ij}\partial_{ij}z-\sum_{i,j}(\partial_iA_{ij})\partial_jz.$$

The right side is `L2` and `A33≥alpha>0`, giving the remaining derivative. Interior patches permit all quotient directions. Finite cover and the bounded chart pullbacks give the global natural-boundary `H2` estimate with the displayed data norms and `||w||H1`.

**Every higher order, without pretending Neumann derivatives keep zero flux.** If `w∈H^{k+1}` and its smooth homogeneous-Neumann equation has datum in `H^k`, localize as above; the localized scalar datum lies in `H^k`, and its vector datum lies in `H^{k+1}`. Tangentially differentiate by a multi-index `alpha` of order `k`. The resulting weak identity for `D_tan^alpha z∈H1` keeps principal matrix `A`, with scalar datum `D_tan^alpha p∈L2` and vector datum

$$D_{\rm tan}^\alpha G-\sum_{0<\beta\le\alpha}{\alpha\choose\beta}(D_{\rm tan}^\beta A)\nabla D_{\rm tan}^{\alpha-\beta}z.$$

This vector datum is `H1`: every commutator has at least one coefficient derivative, so it uses derivatives of `z` through at most `k+1`, all available from the induction hypothesis. The coefficient derivatives needed are bounded on the fixed smooth patch. The tangentially differentiated flux need not be zero: it is represented by these vector terms in the **natural weak identity**. The H2 estimate just proved applies to that identity. Tangential testing and differentiation are justified by supported smooth-up-to-boundary approximation; the published half-space extension and whole-space mollification/density interfaces provide the needed `H1` approximants without falsely using `H0^1` density.

This controls order-`k+2` derivatives with at most two normal factors. Expand the strong elliptic equation on the interior of each half-patch, differentiate at total order `k`, and recover successively target derivatives with three, four, ... normal factors by solving for the sole `A33` principal term. Every other derivative of order `k+2` has fewer normal factors; derivatives landing on coefficients use `z` through at most `k+1`. The source derivatives are `L2`. The identities represent global weak derivatives on the open half-patch because every compact test support lies in its interior. Finite cover closes the induction. Thus, for smooth data,

$$\|u\|_{H^{k+2}}\le C_k\bigl(\|f\|_{H^k}+\|\kappa\|_{C^{k+2}(\partial\Omega)}+\|u\|_{H^1}\bigr),$$

where constants include the fixed geometry and `epsilon`. This sufficient, nonsharp estimate is complete for smooth parameter families and does not invoke a nonexistent published Neumann higher-order theorem.

**Strong equation and exact Neumann trace after regularity.** Once the estimates give all spatial orders, Sobolev embedding yields a $C^2$ representative on the closure. The weak equation tested against compact interior smooth functions makes the continuous residual $-\epsilon\Delta u-f$ vanish pointwise: if it had a nonzero value, continuity and a nonnegative bump supported in a small interior ball would give a nonzero test pairing. Apply the first Green identity to the smooth representative and tests obtained from the fixed smooth Dirichlet boundary lift. The weak Neumann identity then gives $\int_{\partial\Omega}(\epsilon\partial_\nu u-\kappa)q=0$ for every smooth boundary test $q$. If that continuous boundary difference were nonzero at some point, a nonnegative chart bump supported where it keeps one strict sign would produce a nonzero boundary integral (the smooth chart area Jacobian is positive). Thus the classical conormal equality is exact. This argument recovers the strong boundary condition from the natural weak formulation rather than presupposing it.

**Joint smoothness and the actual neighbourhood.** Differences and time derivatives of compatible data stay in the same compatible linear data space. Weak H1 continuity follows from the energy estimate. Applying the higher-order estimate to a difference quotient minus the solution for the derivative data makes that error tend to zero in every `H^m` on compact time patches, since bulk derivatives converge in `H^k`, boundary derivatives converge in the finite `C^{k+2}` seminorm, and the H1 error tends to zero. Induction gives all time derivatives as solutions for the differentiated data. Higher-order Sobolev embedding gives one consistent family of all mixed boundary jets; the first new parameter-preserving extension lemma then supplies a single smooth ambient continuation. Dirichlet families follow the same argument with the fixed Dirichlet lift and zero-trace operator. This proves both parameter branches of the second supplier.

items.title: Classical elliptic regularity on smooth domains and across smooth interfaces
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice inherited from the stated weak-existence, Sobolev extension and trace suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain, let $\varepsilon\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega;\operatorname{Sym}^3)$ be uniformly positive, and let $\rho$ be smooth on the closure. Prescribe in the prescribed-data lemma either smooth Dirichlet data $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega)$, or smooth outward flux data $g$ with its compatibility condition as in the weak Neumann lemma. Then the weak solution of $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon\nabla u)=\rho$ in $\Omega$ with those data is $C^\infty$ on the closure $\overline\Omega$. For finitely many disjoint closed smooth interfaces strictly inside $\Omega$, piecewise smooth positive $\varepsilon$, piecewise smooth $\rho$ and smooth sheet charge $\sigma$, the weak solution is smooth on each closed side. Edge and junction points, reentrant corners and coefficient loss of regularity are excluded. The existence claims are those of the two weak solvability lemmas; this lemma proves their classical upgrade on the declared domains.
items.strategy:
The existence claims use the AC-qualified prescribed Dirichlet and weak Neumann suppliers; that assumption is transported explicitly rather than inferred from the word "weak solution". Local estimate. In an interior patch, or in a flattened smooth boundary/interface patch, write the weak equation in divergence form $\int a_{ij}\partial_ju\,\partial_iv=\int fv+\int G_i\partial_iv$ with the transformed coefficients $	ilde a=|\det D\Phi^{-1}|\,D\Phi\,a\,D\Phi^{\mathsf T}$; positivity of the Jacobian bounds and the bounds on $D\Phi$ preserve uniform ellipticity. Dirichlet data are removed by subtracting the smooth lift $g(y)\eta(t)$ built from a finite subordinate smooth partition and a normal cutoff; smooth Neumann flux is converted to smooth volume data by a collar vector field $G$ with $G\cdot n=g$ and the divergence theorem. For a tangential direction $k$, put $w:=\delta_h^ku$, and take a cutoff $\eta$ supported in a smaller patch; test the weak identity with $v=-\delta_{-h}^k(\eta^2w)$; change of variables and the product identity give the principal bound $\alpha\|\eta
abla w\|_2^2$ against cutoff terms $C\|u\|_{H^1}[\|\eta
abla w\|_2+\|w\|_2]$, the crucial increment estimates $\|\delta_hu\|_{L^2}\le\|\partial_ku\|_{L^2}$ (from the ACL line identity $\delta_h^ku=\int_0^1\partial_ku(x+	heta he_k)d	heta$, $L^2$ Cauchy–Schwarz on the unit $	heta$ interval and Fubini; the derivative norm is taken on the larger patch containing the shifted segments) and $\|\delta_ha\|_\infty\le\|\partial_ka\|_\infty$, and $f,G$ terms; Cauchy-Schwarz and $2AB\le(\alpha/2)A^2+2B^2/\alpha$ ([[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]]) absorb the gradient terms, giving uniform difference-quotient bounds. The weak second derivatives that are purely tangential (or mixed interior) exist through the bounded functional obtained by passing to the limit of the difference quotients; the Hilbert Riesz representation ([[thm-riesz-representation-for-hilbert-space]]) supplies an $L^2$ representative, with no pointwise derivative or weak subsequence selection. With compactly supported tests the weak identity is $-\operatorname{div}(a
abla u)=f-\operatorname{div}G$ distributionally. Expanding that divergence, at a boundary or interface the normal second derivative is recovered from $a_{33}\partial_{33}u=\operatorname{div}G-f-\sum_{(i,j)
e(3,3)}a_{ij}\partial_{ij}u-\sum_{ij}(\partial_ia_{ij})\partial_ju$ with $a_{33}\ge\alpha>0$. A finite cover of the compact closure gives global $H^2$ bounds on each declared side. The higher-order induction differentiates the weak equation by tangential multi-indices; the exact coefficient commutator is finite and $H^1$, so the same local estimate raises the regularity by two orders of tangential/mixed derivatives, and the normal-recovery equation raises the remaining normal counts one by one; Dirichlet tangential derivatives keep zero trace and natural tests stay admissible. Classical representative: the Sobolev extension theorem ([[thm-extension-theorem-for-bounded-smooth-domains]]) extends each piecewise $H^m$ class to a compactly supported $H^m(\mathbb R^3)$ function, and the Fourier characterisation of integer-order Sobolev spaces ([[thm-fourier-characterisation-of-integer-order-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]]) with Fourier inversion ([[thm-l-two-fourier-inversion]]) converts $W^{m,2}$ membership with $m>j+3/2$ into a $C^j$ representative via the absolutely convergent inverse integral. Derivatives agree with the weak ones by testing and Fubini, representatives agree by continuity, and arbitrarily large $m$ gives a $C^\infty$ representative on the closure whose continuous trace is the prescribed one. Existence of the weak solutions is supplied by the prescribed-data and weak-Neumann lemmas ([[lem-em-prescribed-fractional-dirichlet-existence]], [[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]]).

items.title: Spectral completeness of the curl operator in a smooth PEC cavity
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, as used by the complete variational, Sobolev-extension and compact-spectral suppliers. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain. Define $H(\operatorname{curl})=\{u\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3):\operatorname{curl}u\in L^2\}$ and $H(\operatorname{div})=\{u\in L^2:\operatorname{div}u\in L^2\}$ with their graph norms, and let $X$ be the graph-norm closure in $H(\operatorname{curl})\cap H(\operatorname{div})$ of the smooth fields on the closure with $n\times u=0$; this is an explicit weak perfect-electric-conductor boundary class. Put $V=\{u\in X:\operatorname{div}u=0\}$ and $H=\overline{V}^{\,L^2}$. Then the curl form on $V$ has a complete orthonormal $L^2$ eigenbasis with nonnegative eigenvalues $\lambda_j$ of finite multiplicity tending to infinity whenever $H$ is infinite dimensional, and the zero eigenspace is finite dimensional and must be retained when the topology allows it. Each eigenfield $u_j\in V$ satisfies the full graph-class variational identity $\int_\Omega\operatorname{curl}u_j\cdot\operatorname{curl}v=\lambda_j\int_\Omega u_j\cdot v$ for every $v\in X$. The eigen equation is $$\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}u_j=\lambda_ju_j$$ distributionally with the PEC trace, and for every explicitly chosen mathematical speed $v_{\mathrm{wave}}>0$ and every initial displacement $q_0\in V$ and velocity $q_1\in H$, the associated second-order wave has coefficients $a_j''+v_{\mathrm{wave}}^2\lambda_ja_j=0$ with those initial coefficients. Its displacement lies in $C(\mathbb R;V)$ and its velocity in $C(\mathbb R;H)$; finite modal sums converge respectively in $C(K;V)$ and $C(K;H)$ on every compact time interval $K$. The finite-dimensional $\lambda=0$ sector is retained with $a_j(t)=a_j(0)+ta_j'(0)$. This speed is a positive abstract mathematical parameter, not a physical constant or prerequisite. No identification with every maximal tangential-trace realisation, and no lossy, open or non-smooth-domain spectral claim, is made.
items.strategy:
Compactness and $H^1$ equivalence. For smooth $u$ with $n	imes u=0$, expanding $|\operatorname{curl}u|^2$ and integrating once gives $\int_\Omega(|\operatorname{curl}u|^2+|\operatorname{div}u|^2-|
abla u|^2)=\int_{\partial\Omega}(\operatorname{div}n)|u\cdot n|^2dS$ ([[cor-first-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] and the divergence theorem on the collar). The curvature is bounded on the compact smooth boundary, and the collar normal-line identity $|u(y,0)|^2=|u(y,t)|^2-\int_0^t\partial_s|u|^2ds$ with $2ab\le\delta a^2+\delta^{-1}b^2$ gives $\|u\|_{L^2(\partial\Omega)}^2\le\delta\|
abla u\|_2^2+C_\delta\|u\|_2^2$; absorbing the curvature term yields $\|u\|_{H^1}\le C(\|u\|_2+\|\operatorname{curl}u\|_2+\|\operatorname{div}u\|_2)$, so the completion $X$ is a closed $H^1$ subspace with zero tangential trace by trace continuity. The $H^1$ inclusion in $L^2$ is compact by the elementary cube-averaging proof using the bounded smooth-domain extension ([[thm-extension-theorem-for-bounded-smooth-domains]]): for a bounded family of extensions the rectangular mean estimate gives uniform $\|u-P_hu\|_2\le Ch\|
abla u\|_2$ with $P_h$ of finite-dimensional range, so a finite $\varepsilon$-net exists in total bounded and complete $L^2$. The shifted form $a(u,v)=\int[\operatorname{curl}u\cdot\operatorname{curl}v+\operatorname{div}u\operatorname{div}v+u\cdot v]$ is coercive and complete, so the symmetric solver ([[lem-em-symmetric-coercive-variational-solver]]) defines $K_0$; if $f$ is distributionally divergence-free and $q=\operatorname{div}K_0f$, testing with $v=
abla\varphi$ gives $\int q(\Delta\varphi-\varphi)=0$ for all smooth zero-trace $\varphi$, and the local Dirichlet resolvent and smooth-zero-boundary test-density lemma ([[lem-em-dirichlet-resolvent-h-two-and-smooth-test-density]]) gives the unique $\varphi\in H^2\cap H_0^1$ solving $(1-\Delta)\varphi=q$. Its smooth zero-boundary approximants $\varphi_j$ converge in $H^2$, so $
abla\varphi_j$ are smooth PEC fields converging to $
abla\varphi$ in the curl/div graph norm, proving this gradient belongs to the chosen completion $X$. The identity for smooth $\varphi_j$ passes by $L^2$ continuity to $\int q(\Delta\varphi-\varphi)=-\|q\|_2^2=0$; hence $K=K_0|_H$ maps $H$ into $V$ and is bounded $H	o V$ and compact $H	o H$ ([[def-compact-linear-operator]]). Testing its defining equations with $Kg,Kf$ proves self-adjointness, and $(f,Kf)=\|\operatorname{curl}Kf\|^2+\|Kf\|^2>0$ for $f
e0$ proves trivial kernel. The compact self-adjoint spectral theorem ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-compact-self-adjoint-operators]]) now gives an orthonormal eigenbasis of $H$ with positive eigenvalues $\kappa_j	o0$ of finite multiplicity; substituting $Ku_j=\kappa_ju_j$ into the full $X$ identity gives $\int\operatorname{curl}u_j\cdot\operatorname{curl}v=(\kappa_j^{-1}-1)\int u_j\cdot v$ for every $v\in X$, and testing with compactly supported $v$ gives $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}u_j=\lambda_ju_j$ distributionally with $\lambda_j=\kappa_j^{-1}-1\ge0$, the zero eigenspace being finite dimensional by the spectral theorem. The wave branch is proved for each fixed $v_{\mathrm{wave}}>0$. Equip $V$ with $\|u\|_V^2=\|u\|_2^2+\|\operatorname{curl}u\|_2^2$ (the divergence is zero). It is complete because $V$ is a closed subspace of the graph completion. The full-$X$ eigenidentity gives $(u,u_j)_V=(1+\lambda_j)(u,u_j)_H$, so $u_j/\sqrt{1+\lambda_j}$ is an orthonormal family in $V$. Its orthogonal complement is zero: orthogonality in $V$ forces every $H$ coefficient of $u$ to vanish. [[thm-orthogonal-decomposition-by-a-closed-subspace]] therefore gives completeness in $V$, and [[thm-hilbert-space-fourier-expansion]] yields $\|u\|_V^2=\sum_j(1+\lambda_j)|(u,u_j)_H|^2$. Write $\alpha_j=(q_0,u_j)_H$ and $\gamma_j=(q_1,u_j)_H$. For $\lambda_j>0$, set $a_j(t)=\alpha_j\cos(v_{\mathrm{wave}}\sqrt{\lambda_j}t)+\gamma_j\sin(v_{\mathrm{wave}}\sqrt{\lambda_j}t)/(v_{\mathrm{wave}}\sqrt{\lambda_j})$; for $\lambda_j=0$, set $a_j(t)=\alpha_j+t\gamma_j$. The square roots are those of [[thm-of-square-roots]], and direct differentiation using [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]] and [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] verifies each ODE and its initial values. The positive-mode energy $|a_j'(t)|^2+v_{\mathrm{wave}}^2\lambda_j|a_j(t)|^2=|\gamma_j|^2+v_{\mathrm{wave}}^2\lambda_j|\alpha_j|^2$ has zero derivative by the ODE and is constant by [[cor-zero-derivative-implies-constant]]. The positive eigenvalues are bounded below away from zero, since only finitely many eigenvalues lie in a bounded interval and the zero sector is finite dimensional. Thus this tail energy controls both the $V$ displacement tail and the $H$ velocity tail uniformly in time. The zero sector is finite and has the explicit affine solution. Initial $V	imes H$ summability makes all tails tend to zero; finite sums therefore converge in $C(K;V)$ for displacement and $C(K;H)$ for velocity on every compact $K$, and the series has the given initial data. The uniform limits of displacement and velocity give the actual $H$ derivative: pass the finite-sum FTC estimate ([[thm-ftc-second-part]]) $\|q_N(t+h)-q_N(t)-hq_N'(t)\|_H\le |h|\sup_{s	ext{ between }t,t+h}\|q_N'(s)-q_N'(t)\|_H$ to the limit and use continuity of the limiting velocity. The curl form is bounded on $V	imes V$; uniform convergence on compact times of displacement in $V$ and velocity in $H$ passes the finite equations against a compactly supported smooth time test and a vector in $V$, first for finite eigenfield sums and then by density. Thus the second-order equation holds in the variational, distribution-in-time sense; uniqueness follows from uniqueness of each scalar ODE and completeness of the $H$ eigenbasis. No positive-mode denominator is used for a zero eigenvalue. Positivity of $v_{\mathrm{wave}}$ is essential for the stated arbitrary $V	imes H$ data interface: at speed zero an arbitrary $H$ velocity need not give a $V$ displacement. The spectral, full-$X$ variational, topology and boundary-class interfaces proved above are unchanged.

items.title: Smooth boundary regularity of PEC cavity eigenfields in the declared graph completion
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain, and let $X$ be exactly the curl/div graph-norm completion of smooth-on-the-closure fields with $
u	imes u=0$ defined in [[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]]. If $u\in X$, $\operatorname{div}u=0$ weakly, and $\lambda\ge0$ satisfies $\int_\Omega\operatorname{curl}u\cdot\operatorname{curl}v=\lambda\int_\Omega u\cdot v$ for every $v\in X$, then $u\in H^m(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ for every integer $m\ge1$ and has a $C^\infty$ representative on the closure (indeed a smooth ambient extension to a neighbourhood of the closure). For each $m$, $\|u\|_{H^m}\le C_{m,\Omega,\lambda}\|u\|_{H^1}$. The equations $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}u=\lambda u$, $\operatorname{div}u=0$, $
u	imes u=0$ and $\partial_
u u_n+(\operatorname{div}
u)u_n=0$ hold classically, where $u_n=u\cdot
u$ and the normal is extended constant along collar normal lines. This includes zero eigenvalues and disconnected domains; it asserts neither equality with every maximal tangential-trace realization nor smoothness of arbitrary finite-energy modal sums.
items.strategy:
1. Bilinear boundary identity in the chosen completion. Write $
u$ for the outward unit normal, extend it smoothly as a unit field in a collar, put $\kappa=\operatorname{div}
u$ on the boundary, and write $u_n=u\cdot
u$. Polarizing the identity proved in [[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]] gives, for smooth PEC $u,v$,
$$\int_\Omega(\operatorname{curl}u\cdot\operatorname{curl}v+\operatorname{div}u\operatorname{div}v)=\int_\Omega
abla u:
abla v+\int_{\partial\Omega}\kappa u_n v_n.$$
For clarity the integration-by-parts boundary term before imposing the traces is $\sum_{i,j}\int_{\partial\Omega}(
u_j u_j\partial_i v_i-
u_j u_i\partial_i v_j)$; at the boundary $u=u_n
u$, $v=v_n
u$, the tangential derivatives of $v$ and $
u\cdot\partial_i
u=0$ reduce it to $\kappa u_n v_n$. Thus the sign is positive for an outward convex sphere ($\kappa=2/R$); no convexity is assumed. The $H^1$ norm equivalence of that supplier and the bounded trace [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] extend this identity from smooth PEC approximants to every pair in the actual graph completion $X$. Since $\operatorname{div}u=0$, the assumed full-$X$ eigenidentity therefore gives
$$\int_\Omega
abla u:
abla v+\int_{\partial\Omega}\kappa u_n v_n=\lambda\int_\Omega u\cdot v\qquad(v\in X).$$
This is the weak mixed boundary identity; no classical normal derivative has yet been assumed.

2. Flattening and actual admissibility. Shrink smooth boundary charts before taking a finite cover of the compact boundary, with nested half-boxes and cutoffs away from artificial sides. In each chart choose a smooth orthonormal frame $Q=(	au_1,	au_2,
u)$ on the boundary, by normalizing a graph tangent and putting $	au_2=
u	imes	au_1$, and extend it smoothly into the collar. In flattened coordinates $(y_1,y_2,s)$ with $s>0$ inside, write $u=QU$. The $H^1$ trace has $TU_1=TU_2=0$; $TU_3$ is free. Every localized $H^1$ triple $V$ with these two zero traces and compact support away from the artificial sides pulls back to an element of the original $X$: extend $V_1,V_2$ oddly and $V_3$ evenly across $s=0$. These are $H^1$ extensions. Indeed integrating against a smooth test on both half-spaces cancels the interface term for equal one-sided traces; the odd extensions have matching traces because their traces are zero, and the even extension has matching traces automatically. This is the first-order gluing calculation in [[lem-em-dirichlet-resolvent-h-two-and-smooth-test-density]] and the half-space trace integration argument of [[thm-wkp-extension-from-a-half-space]]. Mollify with a compact kernel even in $s$; convolution preserves these parities, converges in $H^1$, and makes the first two traces exactly zero. Multiply by an even smooth cutoff equal to one on the localized support and pull back through the smooth frame and chart. Extend by zero outside the chart. The resulting fields are smooth on the closure, have $
u	imes v_j=0$ exactly, and converge to the localized field in $H^1$, hence in the curl/div graph norm. This explicitly supplies the smooth PEC approximants required by the definition of $X$. Interior compactly supported tests are obtained by ordinary mollification. This local construction is used below; no equality with an unspecified maximal tangential-trace realization is asserted.

3. The local coupled weak system. Expanding $
abla(QU)$ in the identity of step 1 and transporting the volume measure gives a real symmetric smooth principal matrix $a^{ij}$, uniformly positive on the smaller half-box, that is scalar in the three component indices. The frame derivative terms have smooth matrix coefficients and at most one derivative of $U$. Thus the local equation for all admissible triples $V$ is
$$\sum_m\int a^{ij}\partial_jU_m\partial_iV_m+\int_B eta U_3V_3=\int f\cdot V+\sum_i\int G_i\cdot\partial_iV,$$
where $B=\{s=0\}$, $ eta=\kappa J_B$ is smooth (possibly signed), $f=\lambda JU+\sum_i C_i\partial_iU+C_0U\in L^2$, and $G_i=B_iU\in H^1$ for smooth matrix coefficients $C_i,C_0,B_i$; $J$ and $J_B$ are the positive volume and surface densities. This follows directly by expanding the finite products: the only two differentiated factors produce the scalar $a^{ij}$ because $Q^TQ=I$; terms with a derivative of $Q$ on the test factor enter $G$, and those with a derivative of $Q$ on the solution factor enter $f$. Multipliers obey [[lem-cutoff-difference-quotient-commutator-estimate]]. More generally allow a boundary datum $\int_B hV_3$ with $h\in H^1(B)$ for the induction below. Localization $Z=\eta U$ has the same principal and Robin terms and exactly $f_Z=\eta f+\sum_i G_i\partial_i\eta-\sum_{i,j}a^{ij}\partial_jU\partial_i\eta$, $G_{Z,i}=\eta G_i+\sum_j a^{ij}U\partial_j\eta$, and $h_Z=\eta h$. In particular the divergence-type cutoff/frame terms are retained rather than silently assigning zero conormal data.

4. Tangential mixed $H^2$ estimate. Let $k=1,2$, set $W=\delta_h^k U=(U(y+he_k,s)-U(y,s))/h$, and test with $V=-\delta_{-h}^k(\eta^2W)$ on a nested patch. For each fixed small $h$, its first two traces vanish; step 2 makes its pullback an admissible element of $X$ by actual smooth PEC approximation. Discrete integration by parts and the shifted product rule give the principal term $\sum_m\int\eta^2 a^{ij}(x+he_k)\partial_jW_m\partial_iW_m\ge\alpha\|\eta
abla W\|_2^2$. The other principal terms involve $\delta_h a$, $
abla\eta$, $
abla U$ and $W$ and are bounded by $\epsilon\|\eta
abla W\|_2^2+C_\epsilon\|U\|_{H^1}^2$ on the larger patch. The elementary line formula $\delta_h U=\int_0^1\partial_kU(x+the_k)dt$, valid on a.e. ACL line, and Cauchy--Schwarz in $t$ followed by Fubini give $\|W\|_2\le C\|\partial_kU\|_2$ on the enlarged patch; it also bounds $\|\delta_{-h}(\eta^2W)\|_2$ by $C(\|\eta
abla W\|_2+\|W\|_2)$. Hence the $f$ term is bounded without differentiating $f$. Transfer the quotient in the $G$ pairing to $G$; $\|\delta_hG\|_2\le C\|G\|_{H^1}$ gives the same bound. On $B$ the exact quotient of the Robin product gives $\int_B eta(y+h)\eta^2|W_3|^2+\int_B(\delta_h eta)U_3\eta^2W_3$. The normal-line proof in G3 gives the localized trace estimate $\|Tz\|_2^2\le\epsilon\|
abla z\|_2^2+C_\epsilon\|z\|_2^2$. It absorbs the first term even when $ eta$ has either sign; bounded $\delta_h eta$, $\|TU_3\|_2\le C\|U\|_{H^1}$ and Young bound the second in the same way. The extra $h$ pairing transfers to $\delta_h h$ and is bounded by $\|h\|_{H^1(B)}\|T(\eta^2W_3)\|_2$, again absorbed by the trace estimate and Young. Choosing the finitely many epsilons small relative to $\alpha$ yields
$$\|\eta
abla\delta_h^kU\|_2\le C(\|U\|_{H^1}+\|f\|_2+\|G\|_{H^1}+\|h\|_{H^1(B)}),$$
uniformly for small $h$. These estimates apply to all three components and explicitly bound the coupled lower-order and Robin terms; a scalar Dirichlet theorem has not been substituted for this system.

5. Recover normal derivatives. From the last bound each distributional tangential derivative of $\partial_iU_m$ is $L^2$: for a smooth test $\psi$ its pairing is the limit of $\int\delta_h^k(\partial_iU_m)\psi$, a bounded $L^2$ functional, represented by an $L^2$ class (Hilbert Riesz, available through the variational supplier in G3). Interior quotient tests give the same conclusion away from the boundary. The interior equation is $-\partial_i(a^{ij}\partial_jU_m)=f_m-\partial_iG_{i,m}$. Therefore
$$a^{33}\partial_{33}U_m=\partial_iG_{i,m}-f_m-\sum_{(i,j)
e(3,3)}a^{ij}\partial_{ij}U_m-\sum_{i,j}(\partial_i a^{ij})\partial_jU_m.$$
Every term on the right is $L^2$, and $a^{33}\ge\alpha>0$, so all three normal second derivatives are $L^2$. This proves local $H^2$ with a bound on a smaller patch. It does not require a pre-existing classical Robin derivative.

6. Full bootstrap with boundary commutators. Suppose $U\in H^{r+1}$ on the larger patch, $r\ge1$. Its actual lower-order data satisfy $f\in H^r$ and $G\in H^{r+1}$, since the equation's eigenvalue term is $\lambda JU$ and all coefficients are smooth; no initially smooth right-hand side is presumed. For a tangential multi-index $\alpha$ of order $r$, put $Z=D_y^\alpha U\in H^1$. Its first two traces are still zero. To justify trace commutation, extend any localized $H^{r+1}$ class by the integer-order half-space extension [[thm-wkp-extension-from-a-half-space]], mollify in that norm, and use the continuous $H^1$ trace for every derivative of order at most $r$; the smooth tangential trace identity passes to the limit. Apply tangential integration by parts to the weak system of step 3. Its principal term remains $a^{ij}\partial_j Z_m\partial_iV_m$, its boundary principal term remains $ eta Z_3V_3$, its bulk datum is $D_y^\alpha f\in L^2$, and its divergence-type datum is
$$\widetilde G_i=D_y^\alpha G_i-\sum_{0<\gamma\le\alpha}{\alpha\choose\gamma}(D_y^\gamma a^{ij})\partial_jD_y^{\alpha-\gamma}U\in H^1.$$
The boundary commutator is $\widetilde h=-\sum_{0<\gamma\le\alpha}{\alpha\choose\gamma}(D_y^\gamma eta)T D_y^{\alpha-\gamma}U_3\in H^1(B)$. Indeed $|\alpha-\gamma|\le r-1$, so the indicated derivative of $U$ is $H^2$; its trace and each tangential derivative trace are $L^2$ by the $H^1$ trace and its just-proved commutation. This proves the claimed $H^1(B)$ bound without assuming a stronger trace theorem. Step 2 again makes localized tests for $Z$ admissible by smooth PEC approximation; differentiation of the weak identity is justified first by difference quotients and then distributional limits. Steps 4--5 give $Z\in H^2$, controlling derivatives of total order $r+2$ with at most two normal derivatives. For the remaining derivatives, differentiate the normal-recovery equation of step 5 and induct on the number of normal derivatives at this fixed total order. The non-$(3,3)$ principal terms have strictly fewer normal derivatives; all differentiated coefficient terms use derivatives of $U$ of order at most $r+1$, and differentiated $f$ and $\operatorname{div}G$ have that same available order. Dividing by positive $a^{33}$ recovers the next normal derivative. Thus $U\in H^{r+2}$. Use nested patches for each finite order and the finite boundary/interior cover to obtain $u\in H^m(\Omega)$ for every integer $m$, with $\|u\|_{H^m}\le C_{m,\Omega,\lambda}\|u\|_{H^1}$; no estimate uniform in $\lambda$ is asserted.

7. Classical conclusion. For each $j$ choose $m>j+3/2$ and apply [[thm-extension-theorem-for-bounded-smooth-domains]] and [[thm-higher-order-sobolev-embedding]] componentwise. They yield continuous derivatives through order $j$ on the closure, compatible for different $j$ by weak derivative uniqueness and continuity on the interior. All jets therefore have continuous one-sided boundary limits. The fixed smooth extension [[lem-em-parameter-preserving-smooth-extension-on-a-smooth-domain]] applied to the constant-in-time field gives one actual smooth ambient representative near the entire closure, rather than unrelated finite-order extensions. The interior variational equation gives $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}u=\lambda u$ pointwise, and the tangential trace is classically zero. Now integration by parts in step 1 with arbitrary smooth compactly supported normal boundary traces, admissible by step 2, gives $\partial_
u u_n+\kappa u_n=0$ pointwise. The unit-normal collar extension ensures $\partial_
u u_n=(\partial_
u u)\cdot
u$ when the normal is extended constant along its normal lines. This agrees with the classical identity $\operatorname{div}u=\partial_
u u_n+\kappa u_n$ for zero tangential trace. The argument covers $\lambda=0$, disconnected smooth domains, and every topology allowed by G3; it makes no smoothness assertion for arbitrary finite-energy modal sums. Full AC is carried from G3, the trace, extension, Hilbert and Sobolev suppliers. Hunter's bounded scalar Dirichlet excerpt supports the difference-quotient method only; the vector coupling, actual graph-class tests and Robin bootstrap above are proved locally here.

items.title: Outgoing DtN coefficient at degree zero and the explicit PEC topology zero mode
items.statement: (i) At degree $l=0$ the outgoing radial function of the spherical Hankel lemma is $h_0(z)=-ie^{iz}/z$, so for $k,R>0$ the Dirichlet-to-Neumann coefficient ([[lem-em-outgoing-spherical-hankel-dtn-bounds]]) is $t_0=kh_0'(kR)/h_0(kR)=ik-1/R$: its real part $-1/R$ is negative and its imaginary part $k$ is positive, as the spherical trace lemma requires. (ii) In the spherical shell $a<|x|<b$, the field $u(x)=\operatorname{grad}|x|^{-1}=-x/|x|^3$ is smooth on the closure, nonzero, normal to both boundary spheres, curl-free and divergence-free: $u=\nabla\Phi$ with $\Phi(x)=|x|^{-1}$ harmonic off the origin, so $\operatorname{curl}u=\operatorname{curl}\nabla\Phi=0$ and $\operatorname{div}u=\Delta\Phi=0$ there ([[thm-the-curl-of-a-gradient-vanishes]], [[lem-laplace-fundamental-solution-is-harmonic-off-its-pole]]). Thus $u$ lies in the PEC class $X$ of the cavity spectral lemma ([[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]]) with zero curl, and it has zero curl eigenvalue: eliminating all topology zero modes would incorrectly discard this explicit admissible vector field.
items.strategy: (i) Direct computation: with $h_0(z)=-ie^{iz}/z$, logarithmic differentiation using the algebra of derivatives and the derivative of the complex exponential ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-complex-exponential-is-entire-with-derivative-itself]]) gives $h_0'(z)=h_0(z)\,(i-1/z)$, hence $kh_0'(kR)/h_0(kR)=ik-1/R$ with real part $-1/R<0$ and imaginary part $k>0$; both agree with the exact bounds of the spherical Hankel lemma ([[lem-em-outgoing-spherical-hankel-dtn-bounds]]). (ii) The field $-x/|x|^3$ equals the gradient of $|x|^{-1}$ off the origin; the curl of a gradient vanishes ([[thm-the-curl-of-a-gradient-vanishes]]) and its divergence is the Laplacian of the fundamental solution, which vanishes off the pole ([[lem-laplace-fundamental-solution-is-harmonic-off-its-pole]]); on each boundary sphere $|x|=c$ the field $-x/c^3$ is a nonzero multiple of the outward normal, so its tangential part is zero and it belongs to the weak PEC class of the cavity lemma ([[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]]); its curl is zero pointwise, so it is a nonzero vector in the kernel of the curl form, and such a vector is exactly a zero eigenvalue solution that any complete spectral description of the PEC class must retain.
